scenario: Arguing a nuanced philosophical position
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Úsáidtear é chun tosinseolaíocht nó hipitéis a chur chun tosaigh.

vocabulary.translation: a mhíniú, a chur in iúl
vocabulary.note: Briathar chun cás nó argóint a nochtadh.
Srianann sé éifeacht na rudaí atá ráite.
Smacht smaointe nó tuiscint dhaonna.
Sonrach, i gcoinne ginearálta.

vocabulary.translation: bheith in éide, a bheith agat
vocabulary.note: Bheith in éide cáilíocht nó gné.
Cumais nó acmhainne chun rud éigin a dhéanamh.
Atá mar chuid den rud féin.
Tuiscint ar rud trína sinnse nó trína intinn.
Soiléir a bheith difriúil ó rudaí eile.

vocabulary.translation: mar sin féin, ar an láimh eile
vocabulary.note: Ceanglaítear dhá thosnadh chun iad a choinneáil i gcomparáid.
Tuiscint ar rud de réir do thuairim féin.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I would argue that we shouldn't merely assume that consciousness is a binary state.
dialogue.translation: D'fhéadfainn a rá nach ba cheart dúinn go háirithe a cheapadh go bhfuil an t-aigne ina stáit dhátheangacha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But your claim seems to rest on the notion that it's a spectrum, which is a particular view, not a fact.
dialogue.translation: Ach is é an t-aon rud atá le feiceáil ná go bhfuil do chuid a mhíniú bunaithe ar an tuiscint go bhfuil sé ina speictrim, atá ina tuairim sonrach, ní fíor.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exactly, but I'd say that to possess consciousness is to have the capacity for subjective experience, and that capacity can vary in degree.
dialogue.translation: Go háirithe, ach deirinn go bhfuil an t-aigne ina chumais chun taithí a bheith agat, agus is féidir leis an gcumas sin a bheith i gcéad dream.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So you're saying that this variability is inherent to the phenomenon itself, not just to our perception of it?
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, an bhfuil tú ag rá go bhfuil an t-athrú seo inneallach don tsaothar féin, ní hamháin dár n-aithint air?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Precisely. We perceive different levels of awareness, but that doesn't mean the underlying reality isn't continuous.
dialogue.translation: Go háirithe. Tá aithne againn ar leibhéil éagsúla de chumas, ach níl sé sin a rá gur fíor go bhfuil an fírinne chun tosaigh.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But is that a distinct state from being unconscious? Where do we draw the line?
dialogue.translation: Ach an bhfuil sé sin ina stáit soiléir ó bheith gan aigne? Cá fhad a gcuirfimid srian air?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perhaps it's not a line but a gradient. Whereas a rock has no awareness, a bacterium might have a tiny sliver, and a human has a complex one.
dialogue.translation: B'fhéidir nach srian é ach gradam. Mar sin féin, níl aon aithne ag carraig, ach b'fhéidir go mbeadh sciathán beag ag bacair, agus tá aithne chomhleathaithe ag duine.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But I tend to regard that as a category error. You're conflating information processing with experience.
dialogue.translation: Ach is é a cheapaim ná go bhfuil sé ina mhístuiscint catagóire. Tá tú ag míniú próiseála faisnéise le taithí.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Maybe, but if we don't assume that all complex systems have experience, we still need to explain why some do and others don't.
dialogue.translation: B'fhéidir, ach mura gceapaimid go bhfuil taithí ag gach córas comhleathaithe, caithfimid a mhíniú cén fáth a bhfuil taithí ag cuid acu agus nach bhfuil ag na hinní eile.

scenario: Discussing the limits of free speech
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: úsáidtear é chun rud a theoraint nó a rialú
úsáidtear sé le 'to what extent' chun a fháil amach go dtí cá mhéad
níos fórmála ná 'allow'
fáthanna a thabhairt do rud
comhcheangailt lóiciúil de chúis-toradh

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: To what extent should we restrict free speech when it comes to hate speech?
dialogue.translation: Go dtí cá mhéad ba chóir dúinn saoirse ráiteas a shrian nuair a bhíonn sé i gceist le caint fíorfholláine?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I think we should permit almost everything, but there must be an exception for direct incitement to violence.
dialogue.translation: Ceapaim gur chóir dúinn cead a thabhairt do chuile rud, ach ní mór go mbeadh eisceacht ann do mhíreannaíochta dhreasta chuig fuiléoint.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That sounds reasonable, but how do you justify drawing the line at violence?
dialogue.translation: Fuaimíonn sin go réasúnta, ach conas a dhéanann tú dhlúthús a thabhairt do tharraingt ar an líne ag fuiléoint?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Because violence causes immediate harm, whereas other types of speech can be challenged in the marketplace of ideas.
dialogue.translation: Mar is fuiléoint is cúis do dhíobháil dhreasta, cé go bhfuil cineálacha eile de ráiteas in ann a bheith ina ghaolmhara i margadh na n-aistear.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But hate speech can also cause harm, and it is often a frequent precursor to violence in society.
dialogue.translation: Ach is féidir le caint fíorfholláine díobháil a dhéanamh freisin, agus go minic is é sin tosaí coitianta do fuiléoint sa tsochaí.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That may be true, but imposing restrictions on speech can be abused by those in power. Therefore, we need a very clear and adequate definition of what counts as hate speech.
dialogue.translation: B'fhéidir go bhfuil sé sin fíor, ach is féidir le srianta a chur ar ráiteas a bheith ina n-úsáid chomh fada leis an bhfuil cumhacht. Mar sin, tá a bhfuil ar a dtugtar caint fíorfholláine ag teastáil uainn atá an-soiléir agus i ndea-leith.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Agreed, but I still believe that free speech is a fundamental right, and any restriction must be the exception, not the rule.
dialogue.translation: Aontaím, ach creidim fós go bhfuil saoirse ráiteas ceart bunúsach, agus ní mór go mbeadh eisceacht ann do gach srian, ní rialtas.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I see your point, but protecting minority groups from harm is also essential in a democratic society.
dialogue.translation: Tuigim do bheart, ach tá cosaint a thabhairt do ghrúpaí iarmheiriceá ó dhíobháil riachtanach i dtdhochtúiríocht shochraíoch.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: True, but the overall effect of over-restricting speech might be worse than the harm it prevents.
dialogue.translation: Fíor, ach b'fhéidir go mbeadh tionbhá an fhadhb de shrian a chur ar ráiteas níos measa ná an díobháil a ndéantar é a chosc.

scenario: Analyzing bias in media and journalism
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Tagraíonn sé leanúnas nó dul chun cinn, coitianta i gcur síos ar na meáin.
Tosaíocht an fhaisnéise; riachtanach i nírseoireacht.
Thenéis nó fíricí a thacaíonn le gearán.
Déan rud folamh a dhéanamh folamh, mar shampla bias nó scannal.
Gan páirt a ghlacadh; dealrach i dteoiric don írseoireacht.
Déan bhuntús a chur ar ghréasáin áirithe, go hiondúil ar bhealach roghnach.
Léiríonn sé leanúnas nó patrún coitianta.
Cuir tús áite ar an difríocht nó rud neamhchoitianta.
Déan fíric a mhíniú go bhfuil sé sin amháin agus go bhfuil rud eile ann.
Comharthaíonn an ceann seo toradh nó dul chun cinn.
I bhfíor-chomhcheangal, rud atá folamh nó folamh.
Cuir tús áite ar an difríocht idir dhá tharchlaoiacht.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think we need to expose the bias in this article; it's subtle but pervasive.
dialogue.translation: Creo que necesitamos exponer el sesgo en este artículo; es sutil pero generalizado.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Absolutely. The source they cite seems solid, but the way they highlight certain facts is telling.
dialogue.translation: Absolutamente. La fuente que citan parece sólida, pero la forma en que resaltan ciertos hechos es reveladora.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Right, and they tend to ignore any evidence that contradicts their main argument.
dialogue.translation: Cierto, y tienden a ignorar cualquier evidencia que contradiga su argumento principal.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Despite claiming to be neutral, their language is loaded. It's not merely a matter of tone.
dialogue.translation: A pesar de afirmar ser neutrales, su lenguaje es tendencioso. No es meramente una cuestión de tono.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thus, we need to analyze not just what they say, but what they omit.
dialogue.translation: Por lo tanto, necesitamos analizar no solo lo que dicen, sino lo que omiten.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactly. The real message often lies beneath the surface, in the examples they choose.
dialogue.translation: Exacto. El mensaje real a menudo yace debajo de la superficie, en los ejemplos que eligen.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Whereas one outlet frames this as a security issue, another frames it as a civil rights issue.
dialogue.translation: Mientras que un medio enmarca esto como un problema de seguridad, otro lo enmarca como un problema de derechos civiles.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That framing reveals their core bias, which we can then expose in our own analysis.
dialogue.translation: Ese encuadre revela su sesgo central, que luego podemos exponer en nuestro propio análisis.

scenario: Debating economic inequality and systemic causes
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Tagraíonn sé don airgead a fhaightear, go háirithe ar bhealach rialta.
Acumulación de maoin agus acmhainní, ní iomlán de ioncam amháin.
Difríocht nó distance idir dhá ghrúpa nó méid.
Líne gníomhaíochta nó plean rialtais nó institiúid.
Elementa a dhéanann rann chuid de thoradh.
Deis le húsáid a bhaint as rud nó é a fháil.
Bíonn tionchar aige ar rud nó duine.
Glac le fadhb nó déan iarracht é a réiteach.
Is gá le rud a bheith ann de réir dhlí.
Mór agus tábhachtach go leor.
Léiriú contraste; úsáidtear é le habairt nó fhoirm fhoirfe.
Cuir contras idir dhá tharchlaoi.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The income gap has widened significantly over the last decade, despite overall economic growth.
dialogue.translation: Tá an bhréaga ioncaime tagtha níos leithne i rith na deich mblianta seo caite, fiú má tá fás eacnamaíoch i gcoitinne.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I think the main factor is tax policy, whereas others blame automation for eliminating jobs.
dialogue.translation: Ceapaim go bhfuil an príomhfhachtóir ná polasaí cánach, cé go gcuirfí an bhróisc ar an bhfoghlaim do phost a scriosadh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But automation alone doesn't explain it. The wealthy have far more access to financial instruments that multiply their wealth.
dialogue.translation: Ach ní mhíníonn an bhfoghlaim féin é. Tá rochtain níos mó ag na daoine airgeadais ar ionstraimí airgeadais a fhaigheann a n-airgead.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So you're saying the system requires a fundamental shift, not just tweaks?
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, an bhfuil tú ag rá go bhfuil athrú bunúsach ag teastáil ó an córas, ní hamháin athruithe beaga?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exactly. To address the root causes, we need to reform how capital gains are taxed and ensure fair wages.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Chun na bunús a chur ina luí, caithfimid an córas cánach a athrú agus pá íocta a chinntiú.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But won't higher taxes on the rich affect investment and ultimately hurt the economy?
dialogue.translation: Ach an ndéanfaidh cánacha níos airde ar na daoine airgeadais tionchar a dhéanamh ar infheistíocht agus an eacnamaíocht a bhaint amach i ndáiríre?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Historically, that's a myth. A robust social safety net often correlates with higher productivity and innovation.
dialogue.translation: Stair, is mit é sin. Is minic a bhaineann líonra slándála shóisialta láidir le táirgeacht níos airde agus nuálaíocht.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm not entirely convinced, but you present a strong case. Perhaps we need more data on how inequality affects social mobility.
dialogue.translation: Níl mé go hiomlán sásta, ach tá cás láidir agat. B'fhéidir go bhfuil níos mó sonraí ag teastáil ar conas a ndéanann an comhionannas tionchar ar ghluaiseacht shóisialta.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Agreed. A significant part of the debate should focus on evidence, not just ideology.
dialogue.translation: Aontaithe. Ba cheart go mbeadh cuid mhór den díospóireacht ar an fianaise, ní amháin ar an idé-eolaíocht.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think we should be cautious about genetic engineering, because altering DNA could have unforeseen consequences.
dialogue.translation: cheapaim gur chóir dúinn a bheith cúramach maidir le hinneallacht ginteice, toisc go bhféadfadh athrú ar DNA toradh neamhchoigneoir a bheith air.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But consider the potential to eliminate hereditary diseases. That seems ethical if we can ensure safety.
dialogue.translation: ach smaoinigh ar an gcumas atá ann chun galarthaoinic a scriosadh. Is cosúil go bhfuil sé étice má fhaighimid slándáil a chinntiú.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Safety is a major concern. What if the modifications cause new health risks that we can't predict?
dialogue.translation: is imní mhór é an slándáil. Cad a tharlódh má thugann na hathruithe rioscaí sláinte nua atá againn nach féidir linn a thuairiscint?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: True, but without modification, many people will continue to suffer from incurable conditions.
dialogue.translation: fíor, ach gan athrú, leanfaidh go leor daoine a bheith i do dhiodú ó chiondroma nach bhfuil leigheas orthu.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I understand, yet a widespread use of this technology might lead to inequality, whereas only the wealthy can afford it.
dialogue.translation: tuigim, ach is dócha go gcuirfidh úsáid leathan den tehiceolaíocht seo chun cinn inéacsacht, mar sin féin is iad na daoine airgid atá in ann í a íoc.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's a valid point. We need regulations to ensure fair access to such treatments.
dialogue.translation: sin pointe bailí. caithfimid rialacháin a bheith againn chun rochtain cothrom a chinntiú ar na cóireálacha sin.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, but who decides what is fair? And what about the risk of using this to modify non-medical traits?
dialogue.translation: sea, ach cé a chinneann cad atá cothrom? Agus cad faoi an riosca atá ann ag baint úsáide as seo chun gnéithe neamhleighis a athrú?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We must have an open dialogue and perhaps a global ethical framework to guide these decisions.
dialogue.translation: caithfimid dialúint oscailte a bheith againn agus b'fhéidir straitéis étice domhanda chun na cinntí seo a stiúradh.

scenario: Exploring the tension between tradition and innovation
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: I bhfíor-chiall, glacadh le hiontas le smaoineamh nó athrú.
A choimeád rud i bhfad é féin.
Táirge cultúrtha a fuarthas ó na sineanna.
Díospóireacht fhormhacha nó neamh-fhormhacha faoi théama.
Grúpa daoine a rugadh i gcéim cosúil.
Atá ag tarlú go mall.

Tá sé ina sháinmhíniú ar chomhtháthú nó comhoibriú.
Fhormhach; úsáidtear é chun meicníocht nó próiseas a mhíniú.
A bhaineann le grúpa nó sochaí.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think the shift towards innovation is inevitable, but we need to be careful about the pace of change.
dialogue.translation: Ceapaim go bhfuil an t-athrú i dtreo nuálaíochta neamh-sheallmhar, ach caithfimid a bheith cúramach faoin luí athruithe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Absolutely. However, many people feel that we should preserve our heritage instead of constantly embracing new trends.
dialogue.translation: Go hiomlán. Áamh, cheapann daoine go leor gur chóir dúinn ár n-oidhreacht a choimeád in ionad a bheith ag glaoch ar thréideanna nua go rialta.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a common argument, but the debate isn't just about old versus new; it's about how they can coexist.
dialogue.translation: Sin argóint coitianta, ach ní féidir leis an díospóireacht a bheith faoi shean agus nua amháin; tá sé faoi conas is féidir leo comhtháthú.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: True, but each generation seems to have a different view on this, and that's what makes it so controversial.
dialogue.translation: Fíor, ach tá sé chomh díóscaoilteach sin, toisc go bhfuil dearcadh difriúil ag gach geneamh air.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exactly. I believe the change can be gradual, so that tradition and innovation develop alongside each other.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Ceapaim gur féidir an athrú a bheith cianda, ionas gur féidir leis an sean-nós agus an nuálaíocht a fhorbairt in éineacht.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But sometimes it's not that simple. There are cases whereby innovation directly threatens traditional practices.
dialogue.translation: Ach níl sé chomh simplí sin uaireanta. Tá cásanna ina dtugann nuálaíocht bhrí do chleachtais shean-nósa.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I understand, but ultimately, we need to find a way to integrate the best of both worlds.
dialogue.translation: Tuigim, ach i ndáiríre, caithfimid bealach a fháil chun an fearr d'an dá saol a eagrú.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That requires a collective effort, not just from leaders but from every member of the community.
dialogue.translation: Tá a choimeád ag teastáil ó gach ball den phobal, ní hamháin ó cheannairí.

scenario: Analyzing a historical turning point
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Úsáidtear é le haghaidh imeachtaí a tharlaíonn i gcuid ar leith ama.
Cé go bhfuil sé i gceist liosta a sheachaint cheana féin, cuirtear é anseo toisc go bhfuil sé de thrí do mhórchuid agus go dtagann sé go nádúrtha sa dialúint.

vocabulary.translation: mar thoradh air sin, dá bhrí sin

vocabulary.note: Ceanglaí formal; úsáidtear é chun meicníocht nó próiseas a mhíniú.

vocabulary.translation: ó shin i leith, ón am sin amach

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Let's examine what exactly triggered the shift in public opinion before the revolution.
dialogue.translation: Déanaimis iniúchadh ar cad atá tógtha ar bun go díreach an athrú sa bharúil phoiblí roimh an ghéarchéim.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Well, a significant factor was the economic crisis that occurred in the prior decade, which undermined trust in the monarchy.
dialogue.translation: Go maith, bhí bhunús mhór ann mar gheall ar an gcéad chéad bliain roimh ré, a chuir lagú ar an muinín sa ríocht.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That makes sense. But did the subsequent reforms manage to restore stability?
dialogue.translation: Sin ciallmhar. Ach an bhfuair na hathruithe ina dhiaidh sin an stádas a athshlánaigh?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not really. The reforms were too superficial; they failed to address the underlying notion of inequality, and consequently, the unrest persisted.
dialogue.translation: Ní go hiomlán. Bhí na hathruithe ró-shimplí; theip orthu an tuiscint bunúsach de mhí-ionchas a chur ina luí, agus mar thoradh air sin, lean an t-éagóir ar aghaidh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So, the turning point was the failure of those reforms, whereby the people realized that only a complete overhaul could prevail.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, bhí an pointe athruithe i mbun an bhuachan, ar bhealach a d'fhéadfadh an pobal a bheith ar an eolas nach raibh ach athshlánaithe iomlán in ann bua a fháil.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactly. And henceforth, the idea of a republic gained momentum, leading to the eventual overthrow of the regime.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Agus ón am sin amach, fuair an smaoineamh de phoblachta cumhacht, a d'ainmigh go deo an réimeas a bhriseadh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What was the final outcome of that process? Did the new government meet the people's expectations?
dialogue.translation: Cad a bhí mar thoradh deiridh ar an bpróiseas sin? An bhfuair an rialtas nua na haon tréith a bhí ag an bpobal?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: The outcome was mixed; although the republic was established, internal conflicts soon emerged, and the initial ideals began to fade.
dialogue.translation: Bhí an toradh comhiomlán; cé go raibh an phoblachta bunaithe, d'éirigh géarchéim intiuil go tapaidh, agus thosaigh na dealraithe tosaigh ag éirí as cionn.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It seems that the turning point, while decisive, didn't guarantee a smooth transition. Let's analyze why that occurred.
dialogue.translation: Is léir go raibh an pointe athruithe, cé go raibh sé cinnte, gan aon bhealach suarach a bheith ann. Déanaimis iniúchadh ar an gcéad uair a tharla sé.

vocabulary.translation: leithéid a dhéanamh, a thabhairt le fios
vocabulary.note: Ná déan dearmad é a chur i gcomparáid le 'infer' (infear).
Le haghaidh scileanna meabhracha nó fisiciúla.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I've been thinking about consciousness lately. Do you think we can ever fully perceive what another mind is experiencing?
dialogue.translation: Tá mé ag smaoineamh ar an ndóchas le déanaí. An smaoiníonn tú gur féidir linn a bheith iomlán tuiscint a fháil ar an rud atá eile a thaithí?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's a tricky question. We can be aware of our own experiences, but the gap between minds seems inherent to the human condition.
dialogue.translation: Sin ceist deacair. Is féidir linn a bheith ar an eolas faoi ár gcuid taithí féin, ach is cosúil go bhfuil an bhealach idir intinn inneallach don chomhaireamh daonna.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Right, but some philosophers argue that consciousness might arise from purely physical processes in the brain. How do you see that?
dialogue.translation: Ceart go leor, ach deir roinnt fealsúnóirí go bhféadfadh an dóchas a tharlú as próisis fhíor-fhisiciúla sa bhrain. Conas a fheic tú sin?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I find that somewhat plausible, but it depends on the frame you use. If you assume a purely materialist frame, then yes, but that assumption might be too limiting.
dialogue.translation: Is féidir liom é a bheith i gceist beagán, ach is faoi leithéid an chreat a úsáideann tú. Má cheapann tú creat fhíor-mhíochaineach, ansin sea, ach d'fhéadfadh an meabhrú sin a bheith ró- teoranta.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So you're saying the way we define consciousness influences what we find? That implies a crucial subjective element, doesn't it?
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, tá tú ag rá go bhfuil an bealach a ndéantar againn an dóchas a shainmhíníonn cad a fhaightear againn? Tugann sin le fios go bhfuil sé riachtanach go bhfuil sé riachtanach, nach bhfuil?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactly. And there's also the question of whether consciousness has a unique dimension beyond the physical. Some call it the 'hard problem'.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Agus tá ceist ann freisin an bhfuil dimensiún uathúil ag an ndóchas thar an ghnéas. Glaoigh roinnt air an 'fhadhb deacair'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But if that dimension exists, how would we ever measure it? Science relies on observable data, whereby we infer mental states from behavior.
dialogue.translation: Ach más ann dó an dimensiún sin, conas a mhéadúidh muid é riamh? Tá an eolaíocht ag brath ar na sonraí a fheictear, ar bhealach a ndéantar againn staid intinne a infheidhmithe as an iompair.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: True, but our capacity to observe is limited. Even in humans, we can't directly access another's subjective experience.
dialogue.translation: Fíor, ach tá ár gcumas a fheiceáil teoranta. Fiú i dtaoibh daoine, ní féidir linn rochtain dhíreach a fháil ar thaithí eile.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So maybe consciousness will always remain a mystery in some sense. But that doesn't stop us from exploring it, does it?
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, b'fhéidir go gcuirfear an dóchas i gcás éigin i gcónaí. Ach ní chuidíonn sin linn é a iniúchadh, nach bhfuil?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think the current justice system focuses too much on punishment rather than on reform.
dialogue.translation: Ceapaim go bhfuil an córas ceartais reatha ag díriú roimh ré soicind ar shásamh i dtionnasc ar athchóiriú.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But what about the victims? For serious crimes, a harsh penalty seems necessary to punish the offender.
dialogue.translation: Ach céard faoi na hiontaigh? Do choireachtaí tromchúiseacha, is cosúil go gcaithfear péin trom a thabhairt chun an coiriteoir a shásamh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I agree that some offenses deserve severe sentences, but we also need to consider rehabilitation.
dialogue.translation: Tá mé d'aois gur cheart go mbeadh abairtí tromchúiseacha ag cuid uafása, ach caithfimid smaoineamh ar athshlánú chomh maith.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: However, if someone is found guilty of a violent crime, the trial must ensure that the sentence fits the offense.
dialogue.translation: Áfach, má bhéarfar duine ciona de choir thromchúiseach, ní mór don triail a chinntiú go bhfuil an abairt i gceart don uafás.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, but the evidence presented in court is often flawed, and sometimes the jury gets it wrong.
dialogue.translation: Sea, ach is minic is faoi bhun fiúntais atá sa chúirt, agus is minic a bhíonn an giúiré i bhfad uirthi.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's why we have appeals. The system isn't perfect, but it's better than letting criminals walk free.
dialogue.translation: Sin an fáth go bhfuil achomharcanna againn. Ní hé an córas is fearr é, ach is fearr é ná ligint do choiriteoirí siúl saor in aisce.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Still, many experts argue that we should focus on preventing crime rather than just increasing penalties.
dialogue.translation: Foss, argóin go leor saineolaithe gur cheart dúinn díriú ar chion a chosc in ionad péine a mhéadú amháin.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Prevention is key, but without a credible threat of punishment, the justice system would lose its deterrent effect.
dialogue.translation: Is é an cosaint an t-aon rud, ach gan bheith in ann sásamh a thabhairt, caillfeadh an córas ceartais a heafect chosc.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: True, but a fair trial and an impartial jury are the cornerstones of justice.
dialogue.translation: Fíor, ach is iad na príomhchúiseanna ceartais triail cothrom agus giúiré neamhpháirteach.

scenario: Exploring the relationship between language and thought

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you think the language we speak can influence the way we think?
dialogue.translation: An smaoiníonn tú gur féidir leis an teanga a labhraímid tionchar a bheith ar an tslí a smaoinímid?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Absolutely, but I'd say it doesn't simply determine our thoughts – it helps shape them.
dialogue.translation: Ar aghaidh, ach deirinn nach ndéantar ár smaointe a shaincheap go héasca – cabhraíonn sé leo a mhonarchéim a thabhairt orthu.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a common view, though some argue that language is merely a tool for expressing pre-existing ideas.
dialogue.translation: Sin tuairim coitianta, cé go dtuigeann cuid gur uirlis amháin é an teanga chun smaointe atá ann cheana a nochtadh.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But if that were true, why do some concepts seem untranslatable? They often reveal how language and thought are deeply related.
dialogue.translation: Ach más fíor sin, cén fáth nach féidir roinnt comharthaí a aistriú? Léiríonn siad go minic conas atá teanga agus smaoineamh gaolta go domhain.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Good point. For instance, the way we express time in English differs from Spanish – thus, our perception of time may differ too.
dialogue.translation: Point maith. Mar shampla, difríonn an tslí a nochtar am sa Béarla ón Spáinnis – mar sin, d'fhéadfadh ár gcéatadán ama a bheith difriúil chomh maith.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactly. Instead of assuming that language is just a mirror, we should consider how it actively reflects and even constructs reality.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. In ionad a cheapadh gur scáthán amháin é an teanga, ba cheart dúinn a bheith ag smaoineamh conas a athbhraigh sí agus fiú conas a dhéanann sí réaltacht a chruthú go gníomhach.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So, you suppose that changing our language could change our thinking patterns? That seems radical.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, an cheapann tú go dtiocfadh athrú ar ár gcuid patrún smaoinimh má athraímis ár dteanga? Ba mhaith liom a rá go bhfuil sé sin rádical.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not entirely, but I do think it's a two-way street. Language shapes thought, and thought shapes language – it's not a one-way influence.
dialogue.translation: Ní go hiomlán, ach cheapaim go bhfuil sé ina bhealach dhá thaobh. Tabhairt monarchéime teanga ar smaoineamh, agus tabhairt monarchéime smaoinimh ar theanga – níl aon tionchar aon tsíoraíochta ann.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Fascinating. I guess we often overlook how much our worldview is filtered through the words we use.
dialogue.translation: Suimiúil. Cheapaim go minic go bhfuil ár radharc ar an domhan críochnaithe trína bhfuil sa bhfocal a úsáidimid.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think art has a unique power to resist authority without saying a single word.
dialogue.translation: Ceapaim go bhfuil cumhacht uathúil ag an ealaín chun díchill don údarás gan aon focal a rá.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Absolutely. When oppression is widespread, a painting or a song can witness the truth and uncover what the regime tries to suppress.
dialogue.translation: Ar dheis is ar dheis. Nuair a bhíonn croílár leathan, is féidir le péintéireacht nó amhrán bheith ina theist don fírinne agus foghlaim ar a dtugann an réimeas do scriosadh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But isn't that too subtle? I mean, many people need something more direct to take to the streets.
dialogue.translation: Ach, nach bhfuil sé ró-shuaimhneach sin? Is é sin atá mé ag rá, tá a lán daoine ag teastáil rud níos díreach chun dul amach ar na sráideacha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It can be bold, yet it works beyond the immediate protest. Art builds resilience over time, shaping how people see the situation.
dialogue.translation: Is féidir é a bheith dána, ach oibríonn sé thar an toirmiasc ar an toirmiasc. Déanann an ealaín fíochmhaireacht a thógáil trí chéile, ag déanamh conas a fheictear daoine an scéal.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So you'd say a mural in a public square can have more impact than a pamphlet?
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, an ndéarfá go bhfuil tionchar níos mó ag mural i gcearnóg poiblí ná leabhrán?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nonetheless, a pamphlet is quick and direct, but a mural stays in the collective memory for years.
dialogue.translation: Ar choinníoll sin féin, tá leabhrán tapa agus díreach, ach fanann mural sa chuimhne coitianta le blianta fada.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But what about art that is so abstract that no one understands it? Does it still serve the cause?
dialogue.translation: Ach, cad faoi ealaín atá chomh abstracht nach bhfuil aon duine a thuiscint? An fhuil sé fós ina sheirbhís don chúis?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sometimes the most subtle forms are the ones that slip past the censors. They can witness the pain without being suppressed outright.
dialogue.translation: Oft, is iad na foirmeacha is suaimhneacha ná sin a théann thar na cionta. Is féidir leo bheith ina theist don tlag gan a bheith scriosta go hiomlán.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Globalization is full of contradictions, isn't it? For example, we often embrace global brands, but we also worry about losing local identity.
dialogue.translation: Tá an domhanúint lán de chontráracht, nach bhfuil sé? Mar shampla, glacaimid marcaí domhanda go minic, ach tá imní orainn maidir le héachtanas áitiúil a chailleadh.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Absolutely. And that's not just a simple trade-off; it entails complex cultural shifts that can be quite profound.
dialogue.translation: Go hiomlán. Agus ní hamháin go bhfuil sé sin mar chomhchoiste; tá athruithe cultúrtha comhcheathraithe ann a d'fhéadfadh a bheith an-domhand.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yet those shifts often yield mutual benefits, albeit with some inevitable downsides.
dialogue.translation: Ní hamháin sin, ach tá buntáistí comhchoiteann ag na hathruithe seo go minic, fiú má tá cúrsaí nach féidir éalú uathu ann.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: True. But the conflict between economic growth and environmental protection seems inherently difficult to resolve.
dialogue.translation: Fíor. Ach tá sé deacair réiteach a fháil ar an dochar idir fás eacnamaíoch agus cosaint comhshaoil.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, and the proportion of people who benefit from that growth is often surprisingly small.
dialogue.translation: Tá, agus is beag an méid de dhaoine a bhfuil buntáistí acu as an fás sin go minic.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So we have a paradox: globalization promises to connect us, thereby fostering understanding, but it also amplifies inequality.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, tá paraidict againn: deimhníonn an domhanúint sinn a cheangal, rud a chuireann tús le tuiscint, ach méadaíonn sé an comhionannas chomh maith.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: And this contradiction is not just economic; it affects how we see ourselves and others.
dialogue.translation: Agus ní eacnamaíoch amháin an conradh seo; baineann sé le conas a fheicimid muidne féin agus daoine eile.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactly. We need to analyze these paradoxes carefully, even if they seem impossible to resolve.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Caithfimid na paraidict seo a anailísiú go cúramach, fiú má shílimid nach féidir iad a réiteach.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Honestly, that's tough. I think we all need to find some angle—maybe the social aspect, or the learning opportunities—that makes it meaningful enough to keep going.
dialogue.translation: Go hiondúil, sin deacair. Smaoiním go bhfuil orainn go léir aon taobh—b'fhéidir an taobh sóisialta, nó deiseanna foghlama—a dhéanann é tábhachtach go leor chun leanúint ar aghaidh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So you're saying that purpose isn't inherent to the work itself, but rather something we create? That sounds like a philosophy of personal responsibility.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, tá tú ag rá nach bhfuil cuspóir intiuil i gceist ag an obair féin, ach rud a chruthóimid féin? Sin cosúil le fealsúnacht freagrachta phearsanta.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactly. And that's why striving for autonomy is so important—it allows us to shape our work in a way that feels fulfilling, rather than just accept a meaningless routine.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Sin an fáth go bhfuil sé chomh tábhachtach sin iarracht a dhéanamh ar neamhspleáchas—ligfidh sé dúinn ár gcuid oibre a dhéanamh ar shlí a bhfuil mothú sásaimh ann, in ionad rudaí gan bhriathar a ghlacadh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I guess that's the real challenge—to find or create purpose in whatever we do. Thanks, this conversation has given me a lot to reflect on.
dialogue.translation: Measaim gur sin an dúshlán fíor—cuspóir a aimsiú nó a chruthú i ngach rud a dhéanann muid. Go raibh maith agat, tá an t-suim seo ag tabhairt go leor dom chun smaoineamh.

key_phrases.translation: meán chun deireadh a bhaint amach

scenario: Debating privacy vs security in the digital age
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Tagraíonn sé seo don faireacháin ar dhaoine, coitianta i gcomhthéacsanna slándála.
Procesas códú eolas chun é a chosaint.
I gcomhthéacs digiteach, lachair slándála.
Breith bhreosla ar nó faireachán a dhéanamh ar go leanúnach.
Cosaint rud ar dhiamháin nó ar ró-chas a dhéanamh.
Dhligthiúrtha nó ina dhiaidh sin de réir dhlí nó eitice.
An focal céanna leis an chéad focal; athdhéanann sé é anseo chun é a fhorbhairt.
Soileireann agus oscailteacht i ngnásanna.
Rialacha nó dlíthe a leanúint nó a chomhlíonadh.
Cúrsa ina bhfuil rud éigin le haghaidh rud eile a fháil.
A bhfuil iontráil ar phríobháideachas.
Freagrach as a gníomhartha.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I understand the need for surveillance to prevent attacks, but where do we draw the line?
dialogue.translation: Tuigim an riachtanas atá ann do faireacháin chun ionchur a chosc, ach cá bhfuil an líne a tharraingt?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's the crux. We need strong encryption to safeguard our data, yet law enforcement argues it hinders their investigations.
dialogue.translation: Sin an príomhphríomh. Codú láidir de dhíth orainn chun ár sonraí a chosaint, ach deir na gardaí go bhfuil sé ag bacadh a n-iniúchadh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But a breach in any system can expose our personal information, making us vulnerable. How can we trust them?
dialogue.translation: Ach is féidir le lachair i gcóras ar bith ár n-eolas phearsanta a nochtadh, agus a dhéanamh go héadrom. Conas is féidir linn iad a bheith i muinín?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: They claim they only monitor suspicious activities, but that seems too broad. Who decides what's legitimate?
dialogue.translation: Deir siad nach bhfuil siad ag faireachán ach gníomhartha amhisniúla, ach is léir go bhfuil sé ró-leathan. Cé a chinneann cad atá dhligthiúrtha?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exactly! We need more transparency about their methods and limits. Otherwise, it's just an intrusive power grab.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach! Níos mó trédhearcachta de dhíth orainn maidir lena gcuid modhanna agus teorainneacha. Mura mbeadh sin ann, ní bheadh ach gníomh iontrálach cumhachta.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I agree. But if we demand they comply with strict rules, will they still be effective in preventing real threats?
dialogue.translation: Tá mé d'aontú. Ach má éilíonn muid orthu rialacha daingne a chomhlíonadh, an mbeidh siad fós éifeachtach chun fíor-thagairtí a chosc?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It's a trade-off: some inconvenience for better privacy. I'd rather have that than a state that watches every move.
dialogue.translation: Is malartú é: roinnt neamhshocair le haghaidh níos mó príobháideachais. Ba mhaith liom sin ná stáit a bhfuil faireachán ar gach gluaiseacht.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: True. But without oversight, even well-intentioned programs can become abusive. They must be held accountable.
dialogue.translation: Fíor. Ach gan faireachán, is féidir le cláir atá le hiontais maith a bheith truaillitheach. Caithfear iad a bheith freagrach.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So, we need both security and privacy, but the balance is delicate. Let's hope our leaders find it.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, slándáil agus príobháideachas de dhíth orainn, ach is délicheadh an eagar. Go ndéanaí ár gceannairí é a aimsiú.

key_phrases.translation: an líne a tharraingt, teorainn a shocrú

scenario: Exploring cultural imperialism and soft power
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Sa chomhaireamh seo, ciallaíonn sé 'a chur in iúl' nó 'ról a ghlacadh'.
Tagraítear do chreideamh nó toghchán ginearálta.
Socruithe rud éigin le neart nó údarás, go minic i gcoinne toil na dtaoibh eile.
Aon duine a bheith sásta rud éigin a dhéanamh nó a chreidiúch tríd a rá.
Sa chomhaireamh seo, tagraítear do shraith cuspóirí nó intinn folaigh nó folaigh.
Tá sé seo a dhéanamh gan deacracht nó gan a bheith ag déanamh aon choinne.

vocabulary.translation: a través de, por medio de
vocabulary.note: Is é an céanna é seo le 'tríd an mheán' nó 'ag úsáid' canál nó modh.
Úsáidtear é chun dhá idirbhearta nó dhá shituas a choinneáil as a chéile.
An t-iompair nó an toil ina bhfuil duine nó rud éigin.
Níor cuireadh aird ar rud éigin nó a fhoircead.
Tá níos mó cumhachta nó níos mó tionchar ná aon duine eile.
Tá sé go daingean ina chuid den rud éigin eile.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I used to readily accept the notion that Hollywood simply reflects global tastes, but now I see it as a form of cultural imperialism.
dialogue.translation: Bhí mé sásta go héasca an toghchán a ghlacadh go raibh Hollywood ag féachaint ar thástái domhanda, ach anois feicim é mar fhoirm de impireacht chultúrtha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactly. It's not just about entertainment; they often impose their values and lifestyle on other cultures via mass media.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Ní maidir le hámharáil amháin é; go minic a luíonn siad a luachanna agus a saol mhodhanna ar chultúir eile tríd na meáin chumarsáide.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But doesn't that overlook the appeal? People aren't forced to watch; they're persuaded by the quality and the stories.
dialogue.translation: Ach, an ndéanaíonn sé sin an t-ámhar a fhoircead? Níor fhorcadh daoine a fheiceáil; tá siad sásta leis an gcaighdeán agus na scéalta.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sure, it's soft power, not coercion. The dominant culture makes its products so attractive that they become the norm.
dialogue.translation: Go deimhin, is cumhacht bog é, ní dhíobh. Déanann an cultúr domhantach a táirgí a bheith chomh tarraingteach sin go n-itheann siad an chaoi.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So, we assume that consumers have a choice, whereas in reality, the entire media landscape is shaped by a few global conglomerates.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, cheapann muid go bhfuil rogha ag na tomhaltóirí, ach i dtreo is go bhfuil an tírghrá ar fad arna fhorbairt ag aon chonglomerate domhanda beag.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: And that's where the agenda comes in. There's a clear bias towards certain narratives, and local voices often get pushed aside.
dialogue.translation: Agus sin an áit a bhfuil an t-aighnéis ann. Tá bias soiléir i dtreo aon scéim éigin, agus go minic a fhaigheann na hathraithe áitiúla a bheith ar an taobh amuigh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But there's a counter-argument. Local audiences often reinterpret these products in their own way, so the influence isn't as direct as it seems.
dialogue.translation: Ach tá aighnéis eile ann. Go minic a athshocraíonn lucht féachana áitiúla na táirgí seo ar a gcuid féin, mar sin níl an tionchar chomh díreach is atá sé ag teacht.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: True, yet the underlying values are still embedded in the content, shaping perceptions unconsciously over time.
dialogue.translation: Fíor, ach tá na luachanna faoi leith go fóill ina gcuid den ábhar, agus ag déanamh de shocruithe gan choinne ar feadh ama.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So, it's a complex interplay of choice and influence, but we can't deny that the playing field is far from level.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, is é an t-idirbhearta comhoiriúnach roghnaithe agus tionchar, ach ní féidir linn a rá go bhfuil an t-aonad i bhfad ó bheith ar an gcaoi.

scenario: Discussing the limits of scientific knowledge
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Úsáidtear é chun tagairt a dhéanamh do theorainneacha eolaíochta nó réimse áirithe.
Dírítear ar rud atá an-cruinn nó go maith sainithe.
Easpa cinnteachta; tábhachtach sa mhodh eolaíoch.
Tugann sé le fios go bhfuil meastóireacht neamh-cruinn ann.
Tagraítear don fhorleathan nó réimse feidhmíochta.
Aithneoi nó ligean le fios rud éigin, go minic le haighneas.
Rud nach bhfuil deireannach, atá faoi leith in athrú.
Rud a ghlactar mar fhabhtha gan fiúntas.
Laghdú nó corraíonn sé go mall.
Ar bhealach soiléir agus díreach.
Rud a shroichfidh nó a choscfaidh.

vocabulary.translation: por el cual, mediante el cual
vocabulary.note: Ceanglaítear modh le toradh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think we often overestimate what science can tell us; there's a clear boundary to what it can explain.
dialogue.translation: Ceapaim go bhfuil muid go minic ag mheas níos mó ar an méid is féidir leis an eolaíocht a rá linn; tá teorainn soiléir ar an méid is féidir léi a mhíniú.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: True, but within that scope, science is incredibly powerful. The problem is that the results are rarely precise enough for every situation.
dialogue.translation: Fíor, ach laistigh de theorainn sin, tá an eolaíocht thar a bheith cumhachtach. Is é an fhadhb ná nach bhfuil na torthaí go leor cruinn do gach cás.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exactly, and that's where the uncertainty kicks in. Even in physics, measurements are only roughly accurate.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach, agus sin an áit a dtagann an easpa cinnteachta isteach. Fiú i gceistí fisiceacha, níl na tomhais ach cruinn go háirithe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'd go further: scientists often have to acknowledge that their models are just tentative, not final truths.
dialogue.translation: Ghabhfainn níos faide: ní mór d'eolaíonta minic aithint go bhfuil a gcuid samplaí prostúil amháin, gan fírinne deiridh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: And that's not a weakness, but it does undermine the common assumption that science gives us absolute certainty.
dialogue.translation: Agus níl sé sin ina lagú, ach is dócha go gcorraíonn sé an ghabháil choiteann go dtugann an eolaíocht cinnteacht chomhlán dúinn.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Right. I mean, even when theories are explicitly stated, they still rely on unspoken assumptions.
dialogue.translation: Ceart go leor. Is é mé an chiall, fiú nuair a nochtar teoiricí go soiléir, tá siad fós ag brath ar ghabhálacha neamh-ráite.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exactly. And there's a practical constraint: funding and resources limit how much we can investigate.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Agus tá srianta praiticiúil ann: sriantaí airgeadais agus acmhainní ar an méid is féidir linn a iniúchadh.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So the scientific method is a process whereby we reduce uncertainty, but we never eliminate it completely.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, is próiseas é an modh eolaíochta ina laghdaítear an easpa cinnteachta, ach ní scriosann muid é go hiomlán riamh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a good summary. We just have to live with that uncertainty and keep asking questions.
dialogue.translation: Sin achoimre maith. Ní mór dúinn fanacht leis an easpa cinnteachta sin agus dul i gcónaí ag cur ceisteanna.

key_phrases.translation: fanacht leis an easpa cinnteachta sin

scenario: Analyzing rhetoric and persuasion techniques
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Úsáidtear é chun tagairt a dhéanamh do mheán chumhachta (e.g., appeal to emotion = iarratas ar an emóiseán).
Gaolach leis an gcridheacht an labhartha (ethos).

vocabulary.translation: chur in chomhthéacs, a chur in iúl
vocabulary.note: Tabhair aire ar shonraí ar bhealach áirithe chun tionchar a dhéanamh ar thuiscint.
Rudaí nach bhfuil soiléir nó díreach, ach atá i láthair.
Ealaín an labhartha nó an scríbhneoireachta de chaoi cumhachta.
Bunn de chuid argóint ar a dtugtar bunús nó suposiciún.
A bhfuil cuma flúirseach agus cumhachta air.
An dearcadh nó an mothúchán a thugann an labharthóir.
Úsáidtear é chun a rá go bhfuil rud amháin ann agus go bhfuil rud eile ann.
Earráid ráitis a dhéanann argóint neamhbhailí.
A bhfuil cumas aige duine a chur chun cinn.
Foirm fhoirmiúil de 'by which'. Nóta: níl sé sa liosta seachadta ach úsáidtear é anseo mar cheanglaí.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you notice how the speaker used an emotional appeal to make his point seem more credible?
dialogue.translation: An bhfaca tú conas a úsáid an labhartóir iarratas emóisiúnta a dhéanamh a dhéanamh a bheith níos mó crédúchánach?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Absolutely. He also tried to frame the issue as a simple choice between good and evil, which is a classic rhetorical trick.
dialogue.translation: Go hiomlán. Rinne sé iarracht chomh maith an cheist a chur in iúl mar rogha simplí idir maith agus olc, atá sé tréimhse réitóreachta clasaiceach.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That kind of framing can be quite subtle, but it's powerful. However, I found his tone a bit too aggressive for my taste.
dialogue.translation: Is féidir leis an chineál sin de chomhthéacs a bheith suaimhneach, ach tá cumhacht ann. Ar aon nós, bhí a tón agam ar bhealach ró-thréanach do m'blas féin.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I see your point. But, was he merely being aggressive, or was that part of a deliberate strategy to seem passionate?
dialogue.translation: Tuigim do bheart. Ach, an raibh sé díreach ag baint leis an bhfuil sé ró-thréanach, nó an raibh sé mar chuid de straitéis toilteanach chun bheith páiseanta?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think it was deliberate. Still, his main premise seems flawed. He never proved that his solution would actually work.
dialogue.translation: Ceapaim go raibh sé toilteanach. fós, is dócha go bhfuil a phríomh-réamhchúis faoi bhrú. Níor deimhnigh sé riamh go ndéanfadh a fhreagra obair go fíor.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactly. That's a logical fallacy. He assumed a cause-and-effect relationship without any evidence.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Sin camchéim loighciúil é sin. D'fhéach sé go raibh gaol idir chúis agus toradh gan aon fiúntais.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Despite that, he was incredibly eloquent. The way he used metaphors and repetition was mesmerizing, even if the logic was weak.
dialogue.translation: Ceadaigh sin, bhí sé fíorchumhachtach go hiontach. An chaoi a úsáid sé méadaí agus athshónuithe a bhí ag déanamh tús maith, fiú má bhí an loighic neamhchumhachtach.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's the danger, isn't it? A persuasive speaker can hide a weak argument behind powerful delivery.
dialogue.translation: Sin an tságaíocht, nach bhfuil sé? Is féidir le labhartóir cumhachtach argóint neamhchumhachtach a chur i bhfolach taobh thiar de thabhairt cumhachta.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: True. We must analyze the rhetoric, not just the words, to see the mechanism whereby they try to convince us.
dialogue.translation: Fíor. Ní mór dúinn an réitóreacht a anailísiú, ní amháin na focail, chun an meicníocht a fheiceáil ar bhealach a, iarrann siad muid a chur chun cinn.

key_phrases.translation: an cheist a chur in iúl

scenario: Exploring the ethics of humanitarian intervention
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Úsáidtear i gcomhthéacs mhíleata nó polaitíochta: 'to intervene in a conflict'.
Ceart stáit a riar féin gan idirbhearta lasmuigh di.
A bhaineann le cabhair do dhaoine i gcríoch.
Tá fáthanna bhailí le haghaidh gníomh a thabhairt.
Neamhchomhlíonadh dlí nó riail.
Atá i gceart bhreis leis an scéal.
Cead nó comhaontú.
Cead oifigiúil a thabhairt.
Déanta ag taobh amháin gan comhaontú le daoine eile.
Tá sí ina measc.
Déantar é a rá gan deimhniú.
Níl aon aird a thabhairt; a fhoirleachán (tá sé seo curtha i gcló i gceann eile, ach úsáidtear é anseo le matáin).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: If we intervene militarily in that country, we risk violating their sovereignty, even with humanitarian goals.
dialogue.translation: Má ndéanann muid idirbhearta mhíleata sa tír sin, is féidir linn a sovéireacht a bhriseadh, fiú le cuspóirí daonlathacha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But the alleged atrocities are so severe that many argue we must act, regardless of sovereignty.
dialogue.translation: Ach tá na hamhrasacha aontaithe chomh tromchúiseach sin go bhfuil a lán daoine ag rá gur foláir dúinn gníomh a dhéanamh, gan sovéireacht a chur san áireamh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Still, without UN consent, any intervention would be unilateral and impossible to justify ethically.
dialogue.translation: Ar aon nós, gan chead na nAontas Náisiún, bheadh aon idirbhearta aonthalaimh agus bheadh sé neamhbhalbh a chur ina dhícheall go háirithe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yet waiting for authorization could mean letting a violation of human rights continue—how do we weigh that?
dialogue.translation: Ar aon nós, d'fhéadfadh fanacht le húdaráis a chiallaíocht a thabhairt ar chead a thabhairt do bhriseadh de chearta daonna a leanúint - conas a mheásann muid sin?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We must ensure any response is proportionate to the threat, but also consider the long-term consequences.
dialogue.translation: Ní mór dúinn a chinntiú go bhfuil aon fhreagra ciallmhar leis an mbaol, ach tosaigh ar na toradh fhadaithe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I agree, but I'm reluctant to let diplomatic delays cause more suffering.
dialogue.translation: Tá mé d'aois, ach táim dífhábhta le ligean don mhoill díplaiméadach níos mó a dhéanamh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We can't overlook the fact that even well-intentioned interventions often create new instability.
dialogue.translation: Ní féidir linn a thrasnú an fáth go bhfuil idirbhearta maith go minic a chruthú nua instéabilis.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So, perhaps we should focus on non-military aid first, but stay ready to intervene if the situation worsens.
dialogue.translation: Mar sin, b'fhéidir go gcaithfimid aird a thabhairt ar chabhrach neamh-mhíleata ar dtús, ach fanacht le haghaidh idirbhearta má mheasann an scéal.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That seems a balanced approach—though it still requires a clear mandate to be legitimate.
dialogue.translation: Tá sé sin cosúil le cur chuige chothrom - fiú má tá sé fós ag teastáil ó chead údarás a bheith ina dhícheall.

scenario: Discussing post-colonial perspectives in literature

vocabulary.note: Cuid a thabhairt i dteannta i mbun díospóireachta nó argóint.
Atá ciall agus atá sé go maith struchtúrtha.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How does the author depict the relationship between colonizer and colonized in this novel?
dialogue.translation: Conas a léiríonn an údar an gaol idir an cóinneoir agus an cóinneoithe sa nuachtán seo?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's quite nuanced—she avoids simple binaries and shows a hybrid cultural space where both groups inevitably influence each other.
dialogue.translation: Tá sé go leor nuance—seasann sí bináirí simplí agus taispeáin sí spás cultúrtha híobartach ina ndéanann an dá ghrúpa tionchar ar a chéile go dearfach.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That reminds me of the persistent legacy of colonial education, which the protagonist tries to resist by reclaiming her native language.
dialogue.translation: Cuimhníonn sé orm d’oidhreacht leanúnach an oideachais choilíneacha, ar mhaithe leis an príomhcharactar a d’fheicthe a dteanga dhúchais a athchoinneáil.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, but some critics contend that her use of English actually appropriates the colonizer's tool to challenge it from within.
dialogue.translation: Sea, ach deir roinnt criticeoirí go bhfuil úsáid a hAnbhileachta ag an údar an uirlis cóinneoiriúil a úsáid chun é a thorthaíocht ó laistigh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I see that argument, yet it raises the question of whether that strategy risks reinforcing the very power structure it aims to undermine.
dialogue.translation: Feicim an argóint sin, ach cuireann sé ceist ann an dtig leis an straitéis sin an struchtúr cumhachta céanna a chur chun cinn ar mhaithe leis an bhfuil sé ag iarraidh a chur chun cinn.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Precisely. The novel offers a coherent critique of nationalism, but it also reveals how it can marginalize internal minorities.
dialogue.translation: Go díreach. Tugann an nuachtán critic comhréireach náisiúnacht, ach léiríonn sé freisin conas is féidir leis a chinneadh ar mhargadh maoinneoirí intiuil.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a crucial nuance—post-colonial identity isn't a single story; it's a mosaic of different voices, each with its own claim.
dialogue.translation: Sin nuance riachtanach—ní hé an t-aon scéal é an t-aithint pós-choilíneach; is mosaic de ghuthaí éagsúla é, gach ceann aige féin.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Absolutely. And perhaps the greatest achievement of this literature is that it compels us to reconsider the very categories we use to define culture and power.
dialogue.translation: Go hiomlán. Agus b’fhéidir go bhfuil an t-éacht is mó den litríocht seo ná go gcuireann sí orainn na catagóirí céanna a athbhreithnú a úsáidimid chun cultúr agus cumhacht a shainmhíniú.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Well said. These narratives don't just describe history; they actively shape how we understand the persistent inequalities that still affect us today.
dialogue.translation: Ráite go maith. Ní hamháin go ndéantar na scéalta seo a shainiú; déanann siad tionchar ar an gcaoi a ndéantar na heacnamaíochtaí leanúnacha a thuiscint a bhíonn tionchar orthu inniu.
